newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-BELLE GRAND SLAM LEADS WHITE SOX PAST INDIANS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-BELLE GRAND SLAM LEADS WHITE SOX PAST INDIANS.

text.p: Albert Belle extended his hitting streak to 22 games with a grand slam against his former club as the Chicago White Sox cooled off the Cleveland Indians with an 8-2 victory on Tuesday.
Belle connected off starter Albie Lopez (2-3) to cap a six-run fourth inning. It was the ninth career grand slam for Belle and second of the season.

Chicago was already up 4-0 when Cleveland intentionally walked slugger Frank Thomas to load the bases. But Belle crossed up the strategy by hitting a 1-0 pitch over the right-field fence for his 10th homer of the season.
"When they walked me to get to him, that really seems to turn him up," Thomas said. "That's the second time this season he has hit a grand slam when a team walked me to get to him."
Doug Drabek (4-3) allowed one run and three hits over seven innings for the win. Lopez surrendered all eight runs and nine hits in four innings for Cleveland.
Jim Thome homered for the Indians, who lost for just the second time in 10 games.
In Boston, Mike Stanley's pinch-hit single in the bottom of the seventh inning scored Darren Bragg with the go-ahead run as the Red Sox edged the Milwaukee Brewers 7-6.

The game was tied in the seventh when Bragg and Wil Cordero singled with one out off reliever Joel Adamson (1-1). Bob Wickman relieved Adamson and Stanley lined a 3-2 pitch to left, scoring Bragg to make it 7-6.
Stanley is 5-for-11 as a pinch-hitter with seven RBI.
Reggie Jefferson had a two-run homer in the sixth and Nomar Garciaparra had a pair of RBI for Boston, which has won four of its last five games.
In Detroit, Justin Thompson allowed two hits over seven shutout innings as the Tigers scored a 6-2 win over the Anaheim Angels.
Thompson (5-3) struck out six and walked three in winning for the third time in his last four decisions. He extended his scoreless streak to 14 consecutive innings.
Travis Fryman staked Detroit to a 1-0 lead with a solo homer in the third as the Tigers scored at least one run in every inning from the third through the seventh.
The Angels were shut out until the ninth when Jim Leyritz hit a two-run homer off Doug Brocail.
In New York, Jeffrey Hammonds belted a three-run homer and Pete Incaviglia delivered a pair of two-run singles to power the surging Baltimore Orioles to a 10-6 victory over the struggling Yankees.

Hammonds gave the Orioles a 3-0 lead in the second with a homer off starter Kenny Rogers (3-3). Baltimore made it 5-1 in the third when Incaviglia singled home Roberto Alomar and Cal Ripken. The Orioles broke the game open with five runs in the fifth, chasing Rogers.
Scott Kamieniecki (4-2) earned the win against his former team, allowing four runs and seven hits over five innings.
In Toronto, Domingo Cedeno had three hits and three RBI and Juan Gonzalez, Rusty Greer and Billy Ripken drove in two runs apiece as the Texas Rangers pounded the Blue Jays 15-5.
Cedeno victimised his former team. He walked and scored in a five-run fourth, doubled in the fifth, tripled home two runs in the seventh and added an RBI single in the eighth.
The Rangers had season highs in runs and hits, producing 16 hits off four pitchers.
John Burkett (4-3) gave up seven hits in seven innings for the win. Jays starter Robert Person (0-3) allowed seven runs on five hits and three walks in just 3 2/3 innings.
In Kansas City, Mark McGwire hit a two-run homer in the ninth and Jose Canseco added a two-run double in a five-run 10th as Oakland rallied for an 8-6 win over the Royals.

Royals manager Bob Boone pulled Jose Rosado, who was working on a one-hitter, after he walked Patrick Lennon in the ninth. McGwire drilled the first pitch he saw from Hipolito Pichardo over the left-field wall to tie the game.
Scott Spiezio's solo shot put Oakland up by one, but Scott Cooper answered with a leadoff homer for the Royals.
The Athletics then scored five runs in the 10th and the Royals responded with three, coming up short.
At Minnesota, Marty Cordova hit a three-run homer and Chuck Knoblauch drew a bases-loaded walk in a six-run ninth as the Twins edged the Seattle Mariners 11-10.

The Twins began the ninth trailing 10-5 but got an RBI double from Rich Becker and a sacrifice fly by Paul Molitor before Cordova tied the game with his third homer of the season off Seattle closer Norm Charlton (2-4).
The Twins then loaded the bases and Knoblauch walked on a 3-2 pitch, forcing home the winning run as Charlton failed to retire a batter.
Rick Aguilera (3-1) tossed a scoreless ninth for the win.
